lessons.title: If … not and Unless: Same Meaning
lessons.content: 'If … not' and 'Unless' have the same meaning: 'except if'. You can convert between the two forms. Place 'unless' before the positive clause to replace 'if … not'.

details.explanation: 'Unless' replaces 'If … not'. The negative becomes positive after 'unless'.
details.example: If it doesn't rain tonight, the match will start at 9. → Unless it rains tonight, the match will start at 9.
details.burmese: Unless သည် If … not နေရာမှာ အစားထိုး သုံးနိုင်ပါတယ်။

details.explanation: Convert 'unless' back to 'if … not' by adding 'not' to the verb.
details.example: You will fail unless you study hard. → You will fail if you don't study hard.
details.burmese: Unless ကို If … not ပြန်ပြောင်းတဲ့အခါ verb မှာ 'not' ထပ်ထည့်ပါ။

details.explanation: Do not use 'will' or 'would' directly after 'unless', just like after 'if'.
details.example: Unless you violate the rules, you will be in trouble.
details.burmese: Unless နောက်မှာ will/would မသုံးပါနဲ့၊ if နောက်မှာလည်း မသုံးပါနဲ့။
